newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 98 -2 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 130 n/c on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Australian cattle market prices were lower in Queensland and New South Wales (NSW) but increased in other states in the latest week.

Lower prices, especially in Queensland, reflect tighter export margins relative to other states, with higher cattle prices. This has made buying in Queensland more responsive to easing U.S. markets in the past fortnight.
The market for Korean steers was the only real bright spot in Australian cattle sales this week.
Buying to fill Korean tender commitments has assisted prices, especially in Queensland, where both over the hooks and saleyard prices firmed, defying the general price trend.
Direct to works price quotes increased by 10 cents a kg dw for grassfed Korean steers and heifers throughout the majority of Queensland abattoirs.
In the southern region, steers are trading at 175 cents a kg dw and heifers at 170 cents a kg dw. NSW and Victorian processors also lifted their offers for cattle with Korean market specifications.

Demand for grinding beef in the U.S. was a little softer in the past week. In the spot market U.S. domestic lean beef prices fell three cents to five cents US a pound, lowering prices for imported product.
However, demand in the forward market was slightly stronger, cushioning the extent of price falls.
The easing Australian dollar also moderated the decline in Australian export prices, which fell just two Australian cents to 230 cents a kg for 90 CL cow beef.
Export prices to Japan remained firm on last week. The weakening in Japanese wholesale prices, seen again this week, should help support increased end user consumption levels.
